chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn 'Abdah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the loan which attracts benefit, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The best of loans is that which attracts benefit.'

key_terms.يَجُرُّ: Attracts or draws (implies yielding or bringing about)

ai.seo_question: Is a loan that yields benefit considered permissible in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) affirms that the best loan is one that yields benefit, challenging the stricter interpretation that any additional gain constitutes *riba* (usury). This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of distinguishing between a fixed, guaranteed interest (which is prohibited) and variable, permissible benefits derived from the utility or goodwill associated with the loan. It underscores the flexibility in Islamic finance, encouraging lenders to seek modest, non-exploitative returns while maintaining the spirit of benevolence.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Safwan, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Muhammad Bin Abdat who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the loan which attracts the benefits. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The best of the loans is that which attracts the benefits’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from ibn Bukayr from Muhammad ibn ‘Abdah who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, if loan attracted benefits.
He (the Imam) said, ‘The best loan is that which attracts benefits.’”
